newsitem.title: KENYA: Feuding Somali warlords unite in aid appeal.
newsitem.headline: Feuding Somali warlords unite in aid appeal.

text.p: Feuding Somali faction leaders Hussein Aideed and Ali Mahdi Mohamed have united to appeal for donors to provide $100 million for U.N. aid agency operations in Somalia.
The office of the U.N. resident coordinator for Somalia in Nairobi issued on Tuesday a joint statement from the leaders endorsing a U.N. appeal for $100.5 million for aid in Somalia this year.

"We urge the international community to fund the programmes put forward in the appeal...to meet basic needs of the people and to respond quickly to drought that has already started taking its toll on the Somali people," the two warlords said.
Aideed's forces hold much of south Mogadishu and Ali Mahdis north Mogadishu. Both say they want peace but their forces have repeatedly fought over the Green Line battle zone dividing the capital.
The U.N. World Food Programme has said the recent harvest following the short rainy season in Somali produced 53 percent less than last year because of delayed and insufficient rains.
U.N. and other aid agencies are assisting people in parts of Somalia hardest hit by drought and are monitoring other areas.

"Provided the appeal is adequately funded, U.N. agencies and our NGO partners are confident we have the means to address emerging humanitarian relief situations and prevent serious slippage of Somalia into another crisis," said Dominick Langenbacher, the U.N. resident coordinator for Somalia.
Somalia has had no central government since the overthrow of late president Mohamed Siad Barre in 1991. Famine fuelled by bouts of civil war killed an estimated 300,000 people in 1992.
